This is an exact-closure attempt after the three scheduled search lenses. Concentrate on resolving the independent audit. If no material proof change is required, copy claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch, and final_writeup from the parent exactly.

      "claim": "Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.",

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For fixed labeled bugs, a feasible code for v is exactly a nonempty subset of A(v). Selecting pairwise-distinct feasible codes is therefore precisely a matching saturating all vertices. Conversely, a saturating matching defines valid monitoring zones. Canonically labeling each enumerated host multiset loses no placements because bug labels are interchangeable. Enumerating all t≤k multisets and testing matching takes f(k)n^{k+O(1)} time.",

    },

      "idx": 1,
      "claim": "Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.",
      "claim_sha256": "fe7f68c0ca461187c0b1dc89fa04000501725922487d3f685d1d093cbda85119",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Every bug appearing in a code of x∈X has its host in N[x]⊆N[X]. With h such bugs, X can receive at most 2^h−1 distinct nonempty codes, proving h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). Bugs cannot operate across components, so every global solution restricts to a solution in each component. Conversely, the union of component solutions is valid because nonempty codes supported on disjoint bug sets cannot coincide.",
      "witness": "The inequalities |X|≤2^h−1 and OPT(G)=sum_C OPT(C) follow directly from code support and disjoint component bug universes.",
      "search_method": "Independent quantifier and component-restriction audit; no external search.",
      "checker_path": "none"
    },
    {
      "idx": 2,
      "claim": "If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.",
      "claim_sha256": "4fc1ce5f32af10ec4f046a3865c087eae974597fe3d362304f7cc19d8f837fce",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Applying claim 1 to X=C gives the component lower bound. Placing h=ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs at a universal vertex makes every nonempty h-bit code available to every vertex, and 2^h−1≥|C| supplies distinct codes. Component additivity gives the stated sum, while components and universal vertices are polynomial-time detectable.",

      "search_method": "Independent lower-bound and constructive upper-bound proof; no external search.",

      "idx": 3,
      "claim": "Let G be formed from a clique C={c_1,…,c_s} by attaching a_i pendant vertices adjacent only to c_i. Then OPT(G)=max{ceil(log2(|V(G)|+1)), sum_i ceil(log2(a_i+1))}; the optimum and a witnessing surveillance system are constructible in polynomial time.",

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "A leaf-hosted bug may be moved to its center without losing its old monitoring zone because N[leaf]⊆N[center]. After all moves, the a_i leaves adjacent to c_i can use only the p_i bugs at c_i, forcing p_i≥ceil(log2(a_i+1)); the global information bound supplies the other lower bound. For K equal to their maximum, partition K bugs into center-hosted groups P_i meeting those sizes. Each leaf group has enough distinct nonempty codes, codes from different groups differ, and at least s of the 2^K−1 codes remain for the clique vertices, which can hear every bug. Scanning at most |V| masks constructs them in polynomial time.",
      "witness": "The checker exhaustively confirmed the formula on 39 small clique-with-leaves graphs; the general construction and lower bounds establish all sizes.",

    },
    {
      "idx": 4,
      "claim": "Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.",

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Double counting gives sum_v|S(v)|=sum_b|M(b)|. Each monitoring zone is contained in the closed neighborhood of its host and therefore has size at most rho, making the right side at most k rho. Since the S(v) are n distinct nonempty subsets of the k bugs, their total size is at least L(n,k).",

      "checker_path": "none"

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",

For P_n, at most k codes are singletons, so total incidence is at least 2n−k, while each bug occurs at most three times; hence k≥ceil(n/2). If n=2t and k=t, equality forces exactly t singleton and t pair codes and every bug to monitor all three vertices around an internal host. Equal or adjacent hosts then create repeated pair codes, so the t hosts would have to be distinct nonadjacent internal vertices, although P_{2t} has room for only t−1. Thus k≥t+1. Reversal changes component order and invokes the reverse local trace, which also costs seven for the symmetric construction. Component additivity gives 3r and 6r optima. This proves the statement for every integer r, not merely sampled values.",

For each tuple, the fixed-placement matching graph has n left vertices and at most 2^t−1≤2^k−1 right vertices, so it is testable in 2^{O(k)} times an input-polynomial factor. Multiple bugs at one host are included by labeled tuples.",
